whatItIs: A multi-host agent-plugin distribution for the Doc Detective doc-testing engine. One source tree (src/) is compiled by build.js (38,468 bytes) into three near-identical published copies (skills/, plugins/doc-detective/) plus host manifests for Claude Code (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json), Codex (.agents/plugins/marketplace.json), Cursor (.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json), Gemini (gemini-extension.json), Qwen (qwen-extension.json) and OpenCode (src/hooks/opencode-plugin.mjs). Contents: 7 skills (doc-testing, generate, init/project-bootstrap, inject/inline-test-injection, test, validate, install-github-action), 6 slash commands shipped twice (.md + .toml), one subagent (src/agents/doc-detective-specialist.md, 14,911 bytes), one Cursor rule (src/rules/doc-detective.md), 5 Edit/Write hooks + a SessionStart installer check (src/hooks/claude-hooks.json), and a remote MCP server at https://agency.doc-detective.com/mcp exposing detect_tests / validate_spec / log_observation (src/mcp-servers.json, src/skills/_shared/MCP-USAGE.md).
method: The encoded method is "Docs as Tests", stated canonically in src/agents/doc-detective-specialist.md lines 89-233 and operationalised by the skills. A document is read as a set of assertions; the unit of assertion is a whole procedure, not a sentence, and each has three parts: action, context, expected outcome (lines 93-106). Procedures, code samples, CLI commands and API calls are declared testable; conceptual overviews and glossaries explicitly are not (lines 108-110). The pipeline in src/skills/doc-detective-doc-testing/SKILL.md line 37 is: interpret doc prose into a Doc Detective spec (a table mapping "Navigate to" to goTo, "Click" to click, "Verify" to find, "Run" to runShell, lines 49-57, expanded in src/skills/doc-detective-project-bootstrap/references/procedure-heuristics.md) then a mandatory schema-validation gate, optional injection of the steps back into the doc source as HTML/MDX/AsciiDoc/XML comments (src/skills/doc-detective-inline-test-injection/SKILL.md), then execution of the literal steps against the real running product, then analysis of testResults-<timestamp>.json, then an optional repair loop. Five tenets (agent file lines 114-122): docs are tests; tests run against the product, not mocks; tests are repeatable; implementation must tolerate contributors who are not engineers; doc tests complement rather than replace unit tests. A validation hierarchy (lines 181-203) ranks deterministic checks (schema, links, UI existence, API status) above grounded LLM checks above ungrounded LLM checks, and sets the migration goal: whenever a probabilistic check keeps checking the same thing, codify it as a deterministic one. For the probabilistic tier it prescribes temperature 0, structured JSON output, confidence bands (auto-pass >=90, human review 31-89, auto-fail <=30), 3-run ensembles with majority vote, and "design tests to flag, not decide" (lines 160-171, 196-201). The rest of the repo is schema drilling: "the action name IS the JSON key, never {\"action\": \"goTo\"}" is repeated in the skill description, the skill body, the agent, the Cursor rule, and is enforced as a PreToolUse blocking hook (src/hooks/scripts/pre-edit-block-action-antipattern.js, 74 lines).
measures: Yes, two things genuinely measure, and neither measures the document as a document. (1) The engine measures the product against the doc's claims: src/skills/doc-detective-doc-testing/SKILL.md lines 139-166 runs `doc-detective --input`, reads summary pass/fail counts and per-step resultDescription, and maps failures back to doc sections; commands/doc-detective-test.md lines 109-118 shows the output shape ("Results: 2 passed, 2 failed"). A doc that is unreadable but factually current passes; a doc with a flawless explanation and one stale command fails. There is no reader, no audience profile, no findability notion, and no coverage metric anywhere in the hand-written sources (grep -rni coverage over src/, commands/, README.md, GEMINI.md, docs/ returns only the word "coverage/" in an exclusion glob and "Broad coverage" in the hierarchy table). (2) A real prompt-level eval exists: src/skills/doc-detective-doc-testing/scripts/test-skill.sh lines 385-675 spawns fresh `claude -p --output-format json --max-turns 5` runs with fixed prompts and scores the replies, printing pass/fail/skip counts and exiting non-zero. That measures the skill file's effect on a fresh model, which is structurally our audit. Its scoring is grep over the transcript and several assertions are weak: Test 14 (line 500) asks the model to restate a rule the skill states, and Test 13 (lines 486-494) passes on a fallback branch whichever way the model answers. Everything else labelled as a number is prescription in numeric clothing: the "confidence" scores in src/skills/doc-detective-doc-testing/scripts/src/fix-tests.mjs lines 31-80 are hardcoded constants per regex error class (element_not_found 70/60/50, timeout 85/75, navigation 90/70, text_mismatch 88) with no calibration data in the repo; the procedure-confidence percentages (90% numbered lists down to 10% FAQs) and the weighted scoring matrix (30/25/15/15/15, thresholds >=4.0 / 3.0 / 2.0) in src/skills/doc-detective-project-bootstrap/references/procedure-heuristics.md lines 16-42 and 196-212 are invented; the similarity scores in src/skills/doc-detective-inline-test-injection/references/markup-patterns.md lines 44-63 (exact 1.0, contains 0.8, overlap 0.1-0.5, order bonus +0.2 / penalty -0.1, match threshold >=0.3) are a real algorithm but they score where to place a comment in a file, not document quality. The repo also ships the two things our evidence already rejected: Vale in CI with a custom house-voice package (.vale.ini lines 12-14, Packages = hawkeyexl/moose-vale, MinAlertLevel = suggestion; .github/workflows/vale.yml, 35 lines) and a structural skill lint (scripts/validate-skills.sh invoking agent-ecosystem/skill-validator --strict).

transferable.approach: Execution-witnessed answer key for command-shaped claims: for every imperative or command block in the .md files, run it against the real build and let exit code plus an output substring/regex be the witness, instead of asking a model whether the doc is true.
transferable.whereItLives: src/skills/doc-detective-doc-testing/SKILL.md lines 139-166 (execute, then read resultDescription per failing step); src/skills/doc-detective-project-bootstrap/references/procedure-heuristics.md lines 95-105 (assert the documented exit-code contract, assert a stable substring or /regex/ of documented output, avoid volatile output, and run against the locally built and npm-linked binary rather than the published package so the test verifies this branch)
transferable.whyItMightWork: Our audit's answer key is derived by reading code, which is a judgement call that a seat can get wrong; an exit code is not. It would make the "lie" class of failure deterministic for exactly the subset of claims that are commands, which in a CLI/plugin repo is most of the install and usage prose.
transferable.collidesWith: audit's answer-key-from-code step, for command-shaped questions only. It does not touch placement or findability, which have no executable witness. It also imports a runtime dependency (the doc-detective engine, Node, sometimes a browser) that our chain currently does not have, and their own SKILL.md line 91 documents that the bundled validator already skews from the installed engine, so the dependency is not free.

weaknesses: It measures product correctness, never comprehension. Nothing in the repo asks who reads the document, whether a reader can find the answer, or whether the answer is there at all; a doc can pass every Doc Detective test while being unreadable, and the only readability instrument shipped is the Vale package our own bake-off beat with unguided controls. The methodology itself lives in an agent prompt, not in code: the validation hierarchy, the confidence bands, the 3x ensembles and "track variance over time" are prose with no implementation anywhere in the tree, and every number that looks measured is asserted (fix-tests.mjs ERROR_PATTERNS lines 31-80; procedure-heuristics.md lines 16-42, 196-212; agent file line 166). Engineering hygiene is poor for something we would lift from: the same instruction file exists three times (src/skills/, skills/, plugins/doc-detective/skills/) and the copies are not byte-identical in a way a path rewrite explains — references/actions.md is 7,476 bytes in src/ and in plugins/ but 7,658 bytes in skills/ (git tree listing), which is hypothesis-level evidence that someone edited the built copy directly; two 2.7 MB bundled validators are committed (doc-detective-validate-test.js 2,750,855 bytes and validate-test.js 2,741,751 bytes) and their own skill file warns they go stale against the installed engine. The whole thing is AGPL-3.0, so the ideas are free to take and the files are not. The PASS/FAIL loop also depends on a live product and, for UI docs, a browser, which is a much heavier harness than our six-question audit.
